rationale: Measured state after the accepted BN-fold bundle (trial-a7f5de7ac7, objective 3.6458 ms vs original 4.2517 ms, decision accepted, quality pass): current discovery on revision 3bd4af68 shows the invocation is GPU-bound (python_runtime-aea48e29: host spends 1.375 ms self in _cuda_synchronize under cProfile; all dispatch - 9x cudnn_convolution_relu 0.456 ms, 11x torch.conv2d 0.326 ms, 3x batch_norm 0.078 ms, 8x relu 0.068 ms - is hidden under GPU execution), so latency only improves by removing/fusing GPU kernel work. Diagnostic CUDA is now 3503.8 us: convolutions 3135.5 us (9 fused conv+relu 1578.1, 8 layer[1] plain conv2d 1459.8, 3 shortcut 1x1 conv2d 97.6), max_pool2d 188.1, 8x aten::add_ 78.3, 8x aten::relu 62.3, 3x shortcut eval-BatchNorm 26.4. The remaining unfused structure is exactly the residual block epilogue: ResNetBasicLayer.forward runs layer[1] conv2d -> residual add_ -> separate relu, and ResNetShortCut runs 1x1 conv2d -> separate eval-BN. Scope selected (joint, 13 module groups whose boundaries together own the whole 3495.8 us ResNetModel subtree except pooling/classifier): the 8 ResNetBasicLayer call sites (4 groups), the 3 ResNetShortCut sites, the ResNetEmbeddings stem site, and the 17 ResNetConvLayer sites whose inherited bundle this proposal explicitly replaces as a whole - the add+relu fusion requires ownership of the layer[1] conv kernel, so partial composition that bypasses only some inherited boundaries is not legal; the new bundle re-implements all 17 folded sites (stem via the embeddings boundary). Replacement: (a) layer[0] and stem stay single aten.cudnn_convolution_relu calls on folded weights, exactly the accepted implementation; (b) each layer[1] conv + residual add + ReLU becomes one aten.cudnn_convolution_add_relu(hidden, W', z=residual, alpha=1, bias=b', stride, padding, dilation, 1) call - this aten op exists in the worker torch 2.13.0+cu129 (schema verified); (c) each ResNetShortCut folds its eval BN into the 1x1 conv weights exactly as the accepted bundle did for ResNetConvLayer, emitting conv+bias in one kernel. Evidence the fused-epilogue cudnn path is the fast engine family here: the accepted trial's parameter search measured cudnn_conv_relu 3.6435 ms vs conv2d_folded 4.2335 ms, and per-shape now the fused op is faster than plain conv2d while doing strictly more work (128ch@28: 149.1 vs 160.4 us; 64ch@56: 230.3 vs 238.7 per call; 256ch@14: 163.6 vs 166.6; 512ch@7: 160.8 vs 164.3). Preserved unchanged: MaxPool2d pooler call (my embeddings replacement calls self.pooler), the 5 nn.Identity shortcut module calls, AdaptiveAvgPool2d, Flatten, Linear, stage Sequential dispatch, no CUDA graphs, no functional dispatch (module-boundary callables only under the legacy backend). Kernel work outside this boundary (188.1 us max_pool2d, 3135.5 us already-one-kernel convs with cudnn.benchmark=False frozen) has no legal eager fusion op, which is why the boundary stops at the block epilogue.
hypothesis: Fusing the residual epilogue into the conv kernel removes the 8 add_ kernels (78.3 us), the 8 post-add relu kernels (62.3 us) and the 3 shortcut eval-BN kernels (26.4 us) - 167.0 us of diagnostic GPU time - and may also switch the 8 layer[1] sites (1459.8 us) onto the faster fused-epilogue engine family (0-7% per-shape advantage observed for cudnn_convolution_relu over plain conv2d). Because the unit is GPU-bound, kernel-time removal translates near-linearly into latency_ms: expect roughly 0.15-0.26 ms improvement from the accepted 3.6458 ms to about 3.39-3.50 ms (4-7%), which is 8-15x the previous MAD-derived noise bounds (0.014-0.021 ms) and keeps images_per_second far above the 7150.1 floor (it rises with the improvement). Numerics: BN folding is the accepted exact reassociation (~1e-7 relative); cudnn_convolution_add_relu computes relu(conv(x)+1*z+bias) with the same single-rounding accumulation order as conv->add->relu, so full 32x1000 FP32 logits should stay well inside atol=rtol=1e-4 with identical top-1, and observe()'s repeated-forward closeness runs the same replaced path. Risks to test on the framework's GPU workers: (1) cudnn 9.20 may not service BiasActivation for every FP32 NCHW shape - mitigation is the accepted pattern: one installation probe plus per-site runtime fallback to conv2d(W',b')+add_+relu_ (kernel-for-kernel the current behavior, no regression), and a route parameter (conv_add_relu vs conv2d_add_relu) so TaskSearch compares routes on paired project measurements; (2) the fused engine for some shape (notably 64ch@56 with z) could be slower than the unfused pair, shrinking or reversing that site's gain - the fallback bounds each site at current cost; (3) z never aliases the conv output (residual is the block input or a fresh shortcut tensor), verified against the transformers 5.16.1 source. These expectations are hypotheses from diagnostic CUDA durations and the accepted trial's measured route effect, not measured clean-timing results; the framework's independent paired measurement decides acceptance.
